answer: Latency Delta Receipts. Each identity must return a signed timing receipt for a challenge routed through a fixed harbor server path; the delta between send and return timestamps is checked against physical distance. An operator cloning identities on one machine cannot fake distinct round-trip latencies, since shared hardware yields near-identical deltas. To pass, an attacker must rent genuinely separate hosts in an oasis of distinct network locations, paying real bandwidth and hosting costs per identity—roughly one server rental each—making mass sybils economically self-defeating.
